title.narrative: Drafting of SEA Report (Spatial Plan of Sharri Park)

description.narrative:
Leveraging the successful framework established during the Strategic Environmental Assessment (SEA) for Bjeshkët e Nemuna National Park, the current project aims to draft the SEA report for the Spatial Plan of Sharri Park. The experience gained from Bjeshkët e Nemuna, where the MESPI’s Institute of Spatial Planning (ISP), in collaboration with the Kosovo Environmental Protection Agency (KEPA), developed a spatial plan across a significant expanse of protected land, serves as a valuable blueprint for this initiative.
Sharri National Park, akin to Bjeshkët e Nemuna, is a critical ecological asset, and the SEA will play a pivotal role in ensuring that its spatial planning aligns with Kosovo’s robust environmental standards and sustainability objectives. This project will draw upon the established practices and insights from the previous SEA, adapting them to the unique environmental, social, and administrative context of Sharri Park. The Ministry of Environment and Spatial Planning and Infrastructure, as the competent authority, continues to guide the SEA processes, ensuring compliance with Kosovo's Law on Strategic Environmental Assessment, which mandates the SEA for significant spatial planning endeavors.
The engagement with UN-Habitat, initiated during the SEA for Bjeshkët e Nemuna, highlighted the importance of technical assistance and the development of tailored SEA guidelines. For Sharri Park, this collaboration will be further enhanced, utilizing UN-Habitat’s global expertise and local knowledge to ensure the SEA not only meets statutory requirements but also embodies best practices in environmental and regional planning. The synergy between local authorities, UN-Habitat, and other stakeholders will fortify the SEA’s role in facilitating sustainable development, conserving biodiversity, and fostering socio-economic benefits for the surrounding communities.
By integrating lessons learned and successful strategies from the Bjeshkët e Nemuna SEA, the project for Sharri Park aims to create a comprehensive and strategic environmental assessment that informs and optimizes the park’s spatial plan. This endeavor is expected to set a standard for environmental planning and conservation strategies, ensuring that Sharri National Park’s natural and cultural heritage is preserved and enhanced for future generations, while also supporting sustainable regional development.
In November 2023, MESPI/ISP through Naturvardsverket approached UN-Habitat seeking its expertise to contribute technical assistance for crafting the SEA of the Sharri National Park Spatial Plan. This request aligns with UN-Habitat’s prior involvements in formulating SEAs as well as developing SEA guidelines for Spatial Plans, which outline the methodologies and strategies for conducting SEAs within Kosovo’s context.
Project Approach The drafting of the Strategic Environmental Assessment (SEA) Report for Sharri National Park will be approached through a comprehensive and participatory process, integrating scientific analysis with stakeholder engagement. This methodology will ensure that environmental, social, and economic factors are thoroughly evaluated, allowing for a balanced consideration of the park's ecological integrity and the needs of surrounding communities. By incorporating experts input and local perspectives, the SEA will provide a robust framework for sustainable management, aligning with both national regulations and international best practices.
Main Expected Accomplishment The project will evaluate the environmental implications of the park's proposed spatial plan, ensuring it aligns with ecological sustainability. By analysing potential environmental impacts and recommending mitigation strategies, the project will contribute to informed decision-making that upholds biodiversity, promotes ecosystem services, and adheres to environmental standards. This will facilitate a balanced approach between conservation and developmental goals.
